task_text: Synthetic binary classification population has 10,000 items, prevalence=0.01, sensitivity=0.9 and specificity=0.95, treated as exact population rates. Return expected_true_positives, expected_false_positives, positive_predictive_value, accuracy, always_negative_accuracy. Under ONLY a prevalence shift to 0.10 with unchanged conditional sensitivity/specificity, return shifted_positive_predictive_value. Separately, a calibrated posterior p is available: a false positive costs1, a false negative costs10, correct classifications cost0. Return positive_decision_threshold (positive if p exceeds it). Return accuracy_alone_proves_usefulness (boolean). Numeric probabilities in [0,1], not percentages.

response.concise_method_summary: Treated prevalence, sensitivity, and specificity as exact rates over 10,000 items. Base case: 100 positives, 9900 negatives → TP=90 (0.9×100), FN=10, TN=9405 (0.95×9900), FP=495. PPV=TP/(TP+FP)=90/585=2/13. Accuracy=(TP+TN)/10000=9495/10000. Always-negative baseline accuracy = 1−prevalence = 0.99, which exceeds the classifier's 0.9495, illustrating the accuracy paradox. Prevalence shift to 0.10 (sensitivity/specificity fixed): positives=1000, negatives=9000 → TP=900, FP=450, PPV=900/1350=2/3. Decision threshold derived from expected-cost minimization with a calibrated posterior p: predicting positive costs (1−p)·c_FP (false-positive risk), predicting negative costs p·c_FN (false-negative risk); predict positive when (1−p)·1 < p·10, i.e., p > c_FP/(c_FP+c_FN) = 1/11 ≈ 0.0909.
assumptions: Given rates (prevalence, sensitivity, specificity) are treated as exact population parameters, yielding exact (non-random) expected counts
Positive decision rule uses strict inequality p > threshold, with p = threshold treated as indifference (not positive)
The prevalence shift affects only the base rate; sensitivity and specificity (conditional on true class) remain unchanged
Correct classifications carry zero cost; costs are additive and linear in classification outcome
Population size 10,000 is used only to compute integer expected counts (TP, FP, etc.); ratios are independent of population size
Posterior p is assumed well-calibrated so expected-cost minimization directly applies
proposed_verification: Check confusion matrix cells sum to 10,000 (TP+FN+TN+FP) in both prevalence scenarios
Recompute PPV via Bayes' theorem: PPV = (sens·prev)/(sens·prev+(1−spec)·(1−prev)) and confirm it matches the count-based ratio
Confirm always_negative_accuracy = 1 − prevalence and compare against classifier accuracy to validate the accuracy-paradox claim
Verify threshold formula p* = c_FP/(c_FP+c_FN) by testing expected cost equality at p=1/11
Re-derive shifted PPV using Bayes' formula with prevalence=0.10 to cross-check the count-based 2/3 result
Sanity-check that increasing prevalence increases PPV holding sensitivity/specificity fixed (monotonicity check)
